title: RapidPnR: Accelerating the Physical Design for FPGAs via Design-Level Parallelism
problem: Physical design (placement and routing) has become a performance bottleneck for large-scale FPGA designs, with runtimes extending design iteration cycles and impacting debugging and optimization efficiency.
motivation: Accelerating physical design is critical to improving FPGA development productivity as circuit designs grow in scale and complexity.
method: The approach automatically divides the circuit design into smaller, independent pieces. Each piece then goes through placement and routing (deciding where components sit on the chip and how they connect) in parallel—all pieces processed at the same time instead of waiting for each one to finish. Once each piece is placed and routed, the results merge back into one complete FPGA design. The entire process runs automatically without any manual work needed.
key_novelty: The core idea is automatically dividing the circuit into pieces so that placement and routing can happen in parallel instead of sequentially.
contributions: Fully-automated netlist partitioning strategy for enabling parallelization
Achieves >50% runtime reduction while maintaining comparable design frequency to commercial tools
Generic framework applicable to large-scale FPGA circuits
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; specific scalability limits, partition overhead, or frequency trade-offs not addressed.
primary_theme: Design-level parallelism for accelerated FPGA physical design
